key_claims: Memory clinics rely on visual rating scales to assess brain atrophy, which lack sensitivity to catch subtle changes associated with early dementia.
A measure of how old a person's brain appears on brain scans compared with their actual age might be a potential predictor of who is more likely to develop dementia over the years.
The study was published in Neurology.
limitations: The source does not provide details on the study design, sample size, or statistical methods.
The source does not specify the time frame for prediction or the accuracy of the measure.
The source does not compare the brain age measure to other diagnostic tools beyond visual rating scales.
what_not_to_say: The brain age measure is definitively predictive of dementia.
The brain age measure is superior to other diagnostic methods.
The study provides causal evidence that brain age leads to dementia.
The study provides specific numbers or statistics about the prediction accuracy.
